questions.prompt: In △ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with DE ∥ BC. Prove that AD/DB = AE/EC.
questions.prompt_markup: In △ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with DE ∥ BC. Prove that AD/DB = AE/EC.
questions.required_method: Prove △ADE ~ △ABC by AA, write AD/AB = AE/AC, then rewrite with AB = AD + DB and AC = AE + EC.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: ∠A shared; ∠ADE ≅ ∠ABC (corresponding angles, DE ∥ BC); AA; AD/AB = AE/AC; so AB/AD = AC/AE, (AD + DB)/AD = (AE + EC)/AE, 1 + DB/AD = 1 + EC/AE, DB/AD = EC/AE, and AD/DB = AE/EC.

questions.prompt_markup: In the proof of the triangle proportionality theorem, the similarity gives AD/AB = AE/AC. Show the algebra that turns this into AD/DB = AE/EC.
questions.correct_answer: Take reciprocals: AB/AD = AC/AE; write AB = AD + DB and AC = AE + EC; subtract 1 from both sides: DB/AD = EC/AE; take reciprocals: AD/DB = AE/EC.

questions.prompt: A proof of the triangle proportionality theorem: 1. ∠ADE ≅ ∠ABC  (?) 2. ∠A ≅ ∠A  (?) 3. △ADE ~ △ABC  (?) 4. AD/AB = AE/AC  (?) Give the reasons.
questions.prompt_markup:
A proof of the triangle proportionality theorem:
1. ∠ADE ≅ ∠ABC  (?)
2. ∠A ≅ ∠A  (?)
3. △ADE ~ △ABC  (?)
4. AD/AB = AE/AC  (?)
Give the reasons.
questions.correct_answer: 1: corresponding angles (DE ∥ BC); 2: reflexive; 3: AA; 4: corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent names for all four.
